_about: What the Windows package holds and the product's own values, the same on every computer (installer\build.py reads it; the paths of the computer that builds are in build.local.json). product: written into setup\manifest.json as it stands, for the setup (Engine.cs) and its page (setup.js): app_folder, the folder an installation goes into; inbox_folder, the folder beside the package and in the installation for model files to sort (named so that nobody takes it for ComfyUI's models folder); workflow_folder, the folder of an existing ComfyUI's workflow list the workflows go into; min_driver, the oldest NVIDIA driver (PyTorch cu130 and llama.cpp's CUDA 13 build both need 580); min_gpu, the oldest NVIDIA cards, as the setup's sentences name them; launchers, a portable ComfyUI's launch scripts, the first that exists starting it; custom_nodes, the custom nodes that ship (folder: about [Chinese, English], what the setup shows of one missing from an existing ComfyUI; why, the reason it ships), every other one is left out and a user adds it through ComfyUI's manager; bundled_models, the folders of the bundled ComfyUI's model library that ship (build.local.json may name others). app: the repository's files the installed program needs (path prefixes, single files). package_licenses: the license files beside the setup. vc_runtime: the Visual C++ runtime files PyTorch and llama.cpp link against, taken from System32 and put beside the programs that load them (Microsoft lets them be shipped with an application); required, those without which the build stops. python_leave_out: what of the program's site-packages stays home. official_workflows: [ComfyUI template, name in the workflow list], the default workflows; templates: where the templates are in a portable ComfyUI. comfyui: what of the developer's ComfyUI stays home, its user's own files: leave_out_app_folders and leave_out_app_files under its ComfyUI folder, leave_out_folders under the portable root, leave_out_names (folder names anywhere), leave_out_files (file patterns anywhere); empty_folders, the working folders that ship empty; user_files, the files of its user folder that ship; manager_update_policy, what ComfyUI's manager is told to follow. comfyui_pip: packages replaced in the copied ComfyUI (build.local.json may name others).

ComfyUI-GGUF.why: GGUF model files (diffusion models, text encoders): ComfyUI's own loaders cannot read them

ComfyUI-PixAI-Tagger.why: the optional "anime to real" workflow, and tagging images
